Clothes & getting dressed

cap noun

headwear

also hat

classical

Traupman 116, 286

1pilleus: double l, short i (the single-l pīleus of Morgan–Owens s.v. hat: cap). Traupman 116, 286, followed here; Lewis & Short’s headword is pilleus too.

pilleus1, pilleī m.

noun, second declension

close-fitting cap or hat, originally of felt

Applied here to modern caps without claiming every modern shape was ancient. A container’s cap or lid is operculum, operculī n., not this headwear noun.

Examples

  • Pilleum indue.

    Put on your cap.composed

  • Ubi est pilleus tuus?

    Where is your cap?composed

See also hat, blender.

SourcesLewis & Short: pilleus · Morgan–Owens: hat: cap · Traupman: Conversational Latin, fourth edition

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
